svg.title: Revision Brand Studio identity and typography v0.2
svg.desc: Experimental identity and typography confirmation board. Compares the current Revision star wordmark, an E-stack/book-stack identity direction, and a Revision plus REV companion lock-up. Also proposes a dual typography strategy: highly readable product text and more distinctive display behaviour.
svg.text: BRAND STUDIO · IDENTITY + TYPOGRAPHY · EXPERIMENTAL
Own the brand. Keep the learning readable.
v0.2 · research only · no identity or font family is approved by this board
RECOMMENDED PRINCIPLE
Revision owns the company identity. REV is a recognisable companion intelligence — related, but not the company logo.
1. Identity directions
Three roles are being separated: current implementation evidence, a proprietary Revision mark direction, and a contextual REV companion lock-up.
IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE
Revision
A · Current Revision✦
Functional and familiar in the learner shell, but the star feels added-on rather than owned.
Recommendation: do not promote as final identity.
STATUS · REVIEW / TRANSITION
RECOMMENDED TO DEVELOP
R
VISION
B · E-stack / book-stack device
The three strokes can read as an E, a stack of books and a signal. It creates an ownable device without making the wordmark noisy.
Recommendation: take this into proper identity design.
STATUS · EXPERIMENTAL / PREFERRED DIRECTION
ALTERNATIVE
Revision
C · Revision + REV companion
Useful in REV-led product, video and campaign contexts. The orb should not replace the core Revision identity.
Use when REV is part of the story.
STATUS · ALTERNATIVE / CONTEXTUAL
2. Small-mark and icon relationship
The system needs a compact Revision mark and a separate REV presence. They should look related without becoming interchangeable.
REVISION SMALL MARK · EXPERIMENTAL
App icon / favicon / social avatar candidate
RELATED, NOT IDENTICAL
REV COMPANION · CURRENT DIRECTION
AI guide / state / motion / conversation identity
IDENTITY RULE TO TEST
Revision is the promise. REV is the intelligence.
The core mark must work without REV. The REV orb may appear beside it when the assistant is genuinely present or being described.
Avoid: turning every Revision asset into an AI-orb asset.
3. Typography strategy
Do not force a single typographic personality to do both dense learning work and expressive brand work.
PRODUCT / LEARNING / ADMIN · RECOMMENDED BASELINE
What matters today?
Readable explanations should stay calm and effortless to scan.
Inter or an equivalently readable modern sans remains a strong baseline for body, controls, forms, learning content and operational interfaces.
Behaviour to standardise
Body 16–18 · comfortable line-height · normal tracking
UI labels 12–14 · stronger weight · restrained uppercase only
Headings compact and confident, never decorative at reading sizes
STATUS · RECOMMENDED STRATEGY, FAMILY NOT FINALLY LOCKED
MARKETING / SOCIAL / VIDEO · DISPLAY VOICE TO EXPLORE
Make the time
you have count.
The board is showing display behaviour — scale, weight, crop and tighter rhythm — not selecting a licensed display font from an SVG fallback.
Selection criteria for a future display family
Distinctive at headline scale · excellent numerals · clear lowercase
Not childish · not institutional · not generic SaaS · strong in video/social
Must coexist cleanly with product body type
STATUS · EXPERIMENTAL / LIVE FONT TEST REQUIRED
V0.2 RECOMMENDATION

Develop the E-stack as Revision's proprietary device; keep REV as a separate companion; retain a readable product type baseline and test a stronger display voice before locking the wider brand typography.
